components.name: Primary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; min-height: 48px; padding: 12px 20px; border: none; border-radius: var(--radius-md, 8px); background: var(--color-primary, #b05740); color: #fffdfa; font-family: var(--font-body, 'DM Sans', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; box-shadow: 0 2px 4px rgba(26,32,44,0.04), 0 1px 2px rgba(26,32,44,0.02); cursor: pointer; transition: filter 300ms, box-shadow 300ms, transform 300ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(0.9); box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgba(26,32,44,0.05), 0 2px 4px rgba(26,32,44,0.03); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #fdf9f0, 0 0 0 4px rgba(176,87,64,0.5); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.95); }

narrative.overview:
The app feels like a good classroom handout printed on warm cream paper: terracotta ink, sage and mustard highlights, and serif headings with a bookish, human feel. It is a modern, phone-first interface, but every surface is tinted warm. Pure white and cold gray are avoided on purpose: backgrounds are cream (`cream-paper`), cards are linen (`card-linen`), and even "white" is an off-white (`off-white`). The result is calm and adult. It respects tired learners instead of shouting at them.

Density is moderate. Cards hold one idea each, there's generous padding (24px), and touch targets are big (48px buttons, 56px bottom nav). Color carries meaning more than decoration. Each activity type (grammar, vocabulary, quizzes, games, speaking, pronunciation) has its own tone family, and each course unit has its own accent. Learners can find things by color before they read the words.

The confirmed anti-references are **cold corporate SaaS** (sterile gray/blue enterprise dashboards) and **kiddie or cartoonish** styling (bubbly, childish game-app visuals). Gamification lives inside the same warm, grown-up material.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream paper ground, never pure white or cool gray
Terracotta primary, sage secondary, mustard accent
Lora serif headings over DM Sans body; Atkinson Hyperlegible available for reading-heavy content
Color-coded tone families per activity type and per unit
Soft, layered, warm-brown shadows; cards lift gently on hover
A separate dark mode on deep navy with a soft sky-blue primary
Phone-first: fixed bottom nav, 44px+ targets, a Large Text option

rules.name: The No Cold White Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are cream, linen or off-white. Pure `#fff` appears only inside form inputs and checkboxes.

rules.name: The Color Means Something Rule
rules.body: Tone families mark activity type and unit accents mark course units. Never borrow a tone color just for decoration, or it stops working as a signal.

rules.name: The Text-On-Fill Rule
rules.body: Filled buttons with text use `terracotta`, `sage-deep` or darker. Mid `sage` (#6a8d73) and `warning-clay` fall below 4.5:1 with white text.

rules.name: The Large Text Rule
rules.body: All type is rem-based. The Large Text setting (`html[data-font-size="large"]`) scales the root to 118.75%, so never use fixed px font sizes for readable text.

rules.name: The Serif Is For Headings Rule
rules.body: Lora is for headings only. Body, controls and labels stay in DM Sans or Atkinson.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are tinted warm brown (`rgba(40,31,23,…)` / `rgba(52,43,34,…)`), never neutral black at high opacity.

rules.name: The Fallback Rule
rules.body: New components pass the light shadow value as a `var()` fallback, and component-specific tokens live in a CSS module next to the component. A missing variable fails silently in production.

dos: **Do** build on the tokens in `src/app/globals.css` (`--color-*`, `--tone-*`, `--unit-*`, `--dashboard-*`), and put new component-specific tokens in a CSS module next to the component.
**Do** use the activity's tone family whenever you show an activity type, and unit accents for course units.
**Do** keep touch targets at 44px or more (buttons 48px by default) and keep the visible terracotta focus ring.
**Do** check every new surface in both light and dark mode, at 320px wide, and with Large Text on.
**Do** respect `prefers-reduced-motion`; the global guard in `globals.css` covers decorative motion.
donts: **Don't** make it look like cold corporate SaaS: no pure white surfaces, no cool gray backgrounds, no sterile blue-gray dashboards in light mode.
**Don't** make it kiddie or cartoonish: no bubbly display fonts, no childish mascots, no candy-colored reward explosions. Learners are adults.
**Don't** put white text on mid `sage` or `warning-clay`, or use `ink-faint` / mustard as text on cream.
**Don't** use fixed px font sizes for readable text; they break Large Text.
**Don't** add new design tokens only to `globals.css` without a `var()` fallback. Stale builds have shipped CSS without the new variables before.
